new_findings.title: CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint fails on the current head, but this predates the base commit and every wave-2 lane inherits it -- not a defect of this lane's fix round or its three tickets
new_findings.evidence: scripts/check-frozen-workflows.selftest.mjs's testCase '(L05-STD-02 fix round) `--ruling` followed by another flag ... is treated as NO ruling given' (line 721) spawns `node check-frozen-workflows.mjs --retire <path> --ruling --child-os` via spawnSync with no env override, so the child inherits the parent's CI=true/GITHUB_ACTIONS=true and hits the CLI's own '--retire is REFUSED under CI' guard before ever reaching the missing-ruling check the cell means to prove, so the assertion on stderr matching /requires --ruling/i fails. Confirmed this exact test case is BYTE-IDENTICAL at the lane's own base commit (`git show 23cfad947b5598214168ba9c43d391b4e16aa745:scripts/check-frozen-workflows.selftest.mjs` contains the same text at the same line), and confirmed the file carries zero diff between the base and HEAD in this lane's branch -- so this is inherited from the wave-1 integrated head, not introduced by any of #846/#782/#988 or by the fix round. It is exactly the failure shape RIG.md's addendum names (a cell green on the rig, red on the runner, PR #1025's own precedent) and none of the three prior review passes nor the fix report itself ran the CI-simulated command (all three reported plain `pnpm lint -> exit 0`).
new_findings.required_fix: Not this lane's fix. The selftest needs to clear CI and GITHUB_ACTIONS for the spawned child in that one cell (or any cell whose refusal sits behind the CI guard), the same pattern RIG.md prescribes. Since scripts/check-frozen-workflows.selftest.mjs is a shared file every wave-2 lane's branch carries unchanged from the same base, this is a wave-wide integration fix, not a per-lane one -- flagging for the orchestrator/integrator rather than requiring lane-03 rework, since lane-03's own three tickets and its fix round never touch this file.
